category: Hype-drop D2C (timed launch, waitlist over always-on)
title: How a Bengaluru sneaker brand turned a 600-pair drop into a 41,000-person waitlist and sold out in 9 minutes at full price
content: A Bengaluru D2C streetwear label was bleeding on always-on Meta conversion ads: CAC had crept to ₹1,150, ROAS sat at 1.8x, and the last 600-pair run took 5 weeks to clear — only after discounting, which was quietly killing the 'hype' positioning the brand sold on. We scrapped always-on and built one timed drop. Two weeks out we ran ₹4.2L of Meta reach+engagement ads (deliberately not conversions) to seed a WhatsApp 'early access' list, gated behind a referral loop (refer 2 friends, skip the queue), and dropped three behind-the-scenes Reels with a Mumbai micro-influencer (88K followers, ₹35,000). Google Search defended the brand term against resellers for ₹40K. The list hit 41,200. Drop day: 600 pairs gone in 9 minutes via a single WhatsApp broadcast link, zero discount. Because the spend built the warm list (not the 600 buyers), effective acquisition cost per waitlister fell to ~₹16 and the cost carried by actual buyers dropped to ₹290; blended ROAS hit 7.5x on ₹51L drop revenue against ₹6.8L total spend. We also captured 40,000+ warm numbers for the next drop — the real asset.
lesson: For any hype or limited-edition model, stop renting Meta to convert on launch day — that is the most expensive minute to buy a customer. Spend the budget two weeks early to build a gated, referral-driven waitlist, so scarcity plus a pre-warmed list does the converting for free. You sell out at full price in minutes instead of discounting for weeks, and you walk away owning a list you can re-drop to at near-zero CAC. Works for sneakers, limited beauty, ticketed events, and any SKU where demand can be time-boxed.
